question: Can the qualified raw-byte motif/adaptive-granularity stack induce a second hierarchy level over recurring morpheme-like compounds and use those structures to generalize a sealed variable-distance reference relation without an external tokenizer?
hypothesis: Across four new seeds, a fixed 16-structure hierarchy learned only from raw bytes will recover all eight level-1 motifs, all four recurring two-motif compounds, achieve >=0.95 local lexicon successor accuracy, >=0.90 long-range reference accuracy on exact compound-pair families excluded from grammar training, beat a motif-only frequency control by >=0.50 reference accuracy, reduce effective grammar-stream events by >=0.30, and use no more than 16 learned structures.

prior_evidence.scientific_claim: Four shared raw-byte motifs transferred zero-shot into a sealed domain; two added target motifs reached perfect accuracy with no source forgetting.

seed_policy: All four seeds were checked against the Wingless repository before preregistration and had no matches. No replacement, exclusion, or extension is permitted.

level1_lexicon.training_record: four motif bytes + deterministic successor + three filler bytes
level1_lexicon.selector: all observed four-byte windows; occurrence>=64; best-successor fraction>=0.90; rank by best-successor count then consistency then lexicographic key; capacity 8
level1_lexicon.prediction: exact learned motif match -> learned best successor; otherwise zero
level1_lexicon.learner_visibility: raw bytes only; record boundaries and motif IDs evaluator-only

level2_compounds.grammar_representation: compound c is the eight raw bytes of its two constituent learned motifs concatenated with no boundary byte
level2_compounds.induction: After level-1 motifs are frozen for the seed, scan grammar bytes left-to-right and emit a motif event whenever a selected level-1 motif matches; otherwise emit one raw-byte event. A level-2 candidate is any two adjacent motif events with zero intervening raw events. Select candidates with occurrence>=64, ranked by occurrence then lexicographic pair, capacity 4.
level2_compounds.hidden_identity: compound IDs/definitions are evaluator-only and unavailable to candidate selection

grammar.record_shape: compound A (8 bytes) + twelve filler bytes + compound B (8 bytes) + one reference byte + three filler bytes = 32 raw bytes
grammar.heldout_rule: pair (A,B) is held out iff (A+B+(seed mod 4)) mod 4 == 1; exactly four of sixteen pairs are sealed from grammar training
grammar.training_schedule: balanced over the twelve non-heldout pairs
grammar.evaluation_schedule: balanced over the four heldout pairs only
grammar.filler: grammar-specific LCG state mapped into 192..255, disjoint training/evaluation initial states
grammar.record_boundary_visibility: no record marker or boundary byte exists; evaluator positions are unavailable to learning

reference_hierarchy.pattern_detection: Using recognized level-2 compound events, collect patterns where two compound events are separated by exactly twelve raw-byte events and the byte immediately after the second compound is the candidate reference target.
reference_hierarchy.first_role_learning: for each first-position compound c, learn one high contribution bit from target-class bit1 by majority count
reference_hierarchy.second_role_learning: for each second-position compound c, learn one low contribution bit from target-class bit0 by majority count
reference_hierarchy.prediction: combine learned first-role bit for compound A and second-role bit for compound B; predicted reference byte=224+(high<<1)+low
reference_hierarchy.structure_accounting: one reference profile structure per compound stores both role contribution counters; capacity 4

controls.motif_only: global reference-byte frequency argmax learned from grammar training; ties choose lowest byte; no level-2 compounds or role profiles
controls.shuffled_compound: deterministically swap the two motif IDs inside every learned compound key for evaluation only; no retraining

event_accounting.level1: each recognized four-byte motif span replaces four raw events with one event
event_accounting.level2: each recognized two-motif compound replaces its two level-1 motif events with one event

budgets.goroutine_policy: single-process deterministic execution; GOMAXPROCS=1 in qualification

validity_criteria: Exact parent SHA, North Star identity, WBG-4 evidence identity, and invalid-R1 supersession match this preregistration.
All four seeds complete frozen lexicon and grammar cardinalities.
Level-1 selection uses only raw-byte window recurrence and successor statistics.
Level-2 selection uses only adjacency of recognized level-1 motif events; hidden compound IDs are unavailable.
Reference learning uses only the frozen twelve-raw-event separation pattern between recognized compounds; evaluator record boundaries are unavailable.
No exact compound-pair reference memorization table exists.
No heldout (A,B) pair appears in grammar training.
Motif-only and shuffled-compound controls receive no extra information or retraining.
The normalized result carries schema wingless.research-scientific-result.v1 and exact experiment identifier.
Full Go regression passes before probe execution.

classification_rules.supported: All sixteen frozen thresholds and all validity criteria pass.
classification_rules.mixed: Hierarchy causally improves sealed long-range reference prediction but at least one recall, accuracy, event-reduction, or capacity threshold fails.
classification_rules.negative: Validity passes but hierarchy provides less than 0.10 long-range gain or fails sealed-pair generalization.
classification_rules.incomplete: Environmental or compute interruption prevents frozen cardinality.
classification_rules.invalid: Provenance, hidden-boundary isolation, heldout leakage, capacity, deterministic construction, or qualification isolation fails.

no_post_result_tuning_rule: After any output is observed, do not alter seeds, motif definitions, compound definitions, grammar shape, heldout rule, reference rule, hierarchy-learning rules, controls, metrics, thresholds, aggregation, or classification.
